content.text: {"overall_verdict":"MEETS_WITH_LIMITED_GAPS","verdict_reason":"The chapter's core additive claims — the kisse'/keseh consonantal identity, the peninim/pearl recovery, and the additive full-moon hearing of the two Proverbs poems — pass the symmetrical admission gate on the same consonants with attested senses, expressly preserve the received readings ('both readings run at once'), and receive noncircular consilience from facts not used to build the background packet (the letter-identical merchandise clause of Prov 3:14/31:18, the Prov 7:20 aleph spelling of keseh, Rev 21:21's one-pearl gates, Ezek 46:1's east gate). However, a small number of outcome-relevant items need documentation or narrowing: the Psalm 81:3 calendrical assertion that the full moon 'is the head of the month' (including the strained 'new-moon trumpet' instrumental rendering) exceeds what the packet establishes and rivals the received calendar without the Rule 4 stage-4 comparison; the Lam 4:7 ruddiness datum against 'pearl' for peninim is unaddressed; and two grammatical claims (Dan 7:9 intensive plural, Aramaic arik sense in a Hebrew poem) lack documented attestation. None of these failures defeats the preserved base readings or the additive symbol; they limit, not overturn, the case.","rule_audit":[{"rule":"1","result":"PASS","reason":"The chapter treats Masoretic pointing as 'a vote, not a veto,' preserves the pointed reading wherever it departs (e.g., kisse'/keseh, shanim/shnayim), and labels its alternates as additional hearings rather than demonstrated originals. It does not demand that the Masoretic reading carry extra burden, and it does not claim its own re-pointings are inspired or confirmed."},{"rule":"2","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"Most citations of Strong's, the LXX, Vulgate, and modern versions are offered as data (attested senses, pre-Masoretic readings). But the Psalm 81:3 paragraph leans on a roll-call of translations ('the NKJV, the ESV, the NASB, the JPS... all read full moon'; 'the King James stands nearly alone') that functions rhetorically as a majority appeal, and many of those versions are not demonstrably independent lineages for this lexical judgment; the underlying lexical evidence, not the count, should carry the point."},{"rule":"3","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"The 'Every Word Weighed' appendix does what the gate requires for most alternates: same consonants, attested sense identified with an independent occurrence (kaph, pelekh, choq via Job 14:13, teref via Ps 111:5, halal via Job 29:3, keseh via Prov 7:20/Ps 81:3). Gaps: the 'appropriateness of days' sense imports Aramaic arik (Ezra 4:14) into a Hebrew poem without addressing language/period applicability; the 'new-moon trumpet' instrumental construal of Ps 81:3 conflicts with the normal idiom taqa' be-shofar and cites no parallel construction; the Dan 7:9 'intensive plural = the wheel complete' invokes no attested grammatical rule."},{"rule":"4","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"The background (moon = faithful witness, gates, twelve; keseh/kisse from ch. 30) is frozen before the target, and the target adds genuinely incremental facts (peninim, the identical merchandise clause, Rev 21:21, Ezek 46:1). But the chapter does not run stage 4: rival joint models (pearl = Christ/gospel; Prov 31 as wife-only; conjunction-start calendar at Ezek 46:1) are never stated at full strength; the keseh/kisse identity established in ch. 30 risks being counted again here; and no reversal conditions are stated."},{"rule":"5","result":"PASS","reason":"The chapter is explicit and disciplined about non-exclusivity: 'Nothing here unseats the wife and mother of the plain reading — both readings run at once'; 'the pointing keeps the housewife; the letters keep the housewife and the light.' It never claims the additive hearing defeats the received reading, and it invites testing rather than declaring victory."}],"claim_ledger":[{"claim":"Hebrew peninim, printed 'rubies' in the KJV, denotes pearls ('probably a pearl (as round)', Strong's), so wisdom (Prov 3:15; 8:11; Job 28:18) and the virtuous woman (Prov 31:10) are priced above pearls, joining the parable's vocabulary.","category":"LEXICAL_OR_GRAMMATICAL","received_or_base_reading":"peninim = rubies/coral (KJV; BDB-line lexica; Lam 4:7 'more ruddy than peninim' suggests a red substance)","proposed_additive_reading":"peninim = pearls (round, white, water-born), keying the Matthew 13 parable to the Proverbs texts","relationship":"CONTRADICTORY_RIVALS","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"PASS","admission_outcome":"UNDERDETERMINED","additive_intent_support":"NOT_APPLICABLE","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"Both senses are attested proposals for a genuinely disputed lexeme, so both pass the gate; but the referent question is a rival-sense contest, not an additive one, and the chapter selects 'pearl' without addressing the strongest counter-datum. Evaluator knowledge (requiring verification): Lam 4:7 predicates ruddiness of peninim, which several lexica take as favoring coral/ruby.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"Lam 4:7 ('more ruddy than peninim') is potential affirmative contextual evidence against 'pearl'; the chapter does not engage it, so exclusion is possible but not established.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A treatment of Lam 4:7 (e.g., ruddiness as glow/luster rather than color, or peninim as a class-term for precious sea-stones) would secure the pearl identification; conversely a demonstration that peninim is color-marked red would break the parable link."},{"claim":"Scripture stamps merchandise 'good' in exactly three places — Prov 3:14, Prov 31:18 (letter for letter the same clause, ki-tov sachrah), and the parable's merchant seeking goodly pearls (Matt 13:45) — binding wisdom, the bride, and the pearl into one thread.","category":"LEXICAL_OR_GRAMMATICAL","received_or_base_reading":"Prov 3:14 and 31:18 are independent commercial metaphors; Matt 13:45 is an unrelated Greek parable","proposed_additive_reading":"The identical Hebrew clause is a deliberate quotation identifying wisdom's and the bride's merchandise, and the parable's 'goodly' merchant joins the same thread","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"PASS","admission_outcome":"BOTH_ADMISSIBLE_ADDITIVE","additive_intent_support":"SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The core textual fact checks out on evaluator knowledge (requiring verification): Prov 3:14 opens ki-tov sachrah and Prov 31:18 contains the identical clause; verbatim clause identity between the two poems is real evidence of intra-book linkage, not mere thematic echo. The exhaustiveness claim ('exactly three places') is plausible (Isa 23:18 predicates holiness, not goodness, of merchandise) but is asserted without showing the search.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None identified.","gap_owner":"EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE_LIMIT","outcome_changing_evidence":"A concordance-complete listing of sachar/sachorah with tov (and the Greek kalos+emporos/margaritēs data) would either confirm or falsify the 'exactly three' exhaustiveness claim."},{"claim":"The consonants of 'throne' (kisse', כסא) and 'full moon' (keseh, כסה/כסא) are interchangeable spellings of one covered/filled root: Prov 7:20 writes the full moon כסא, Ps 81:3 writes it כסה, and Job 26:9 ('he incloseth the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it') survives either hearing — so the throne-word carries an admissible full-moon hearing.","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","received_or_base_reading":"Job 26:9 and Isaiah's 'my throne' read kisse'/kisseh, a royal seat","proposed_additive_reading":"The same consonants also sound keseh, the full moon, so throne texts carry a lunar overtone (Ps 89:36-37 already setting the throne 'as the moon')","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"PASS","admission_outcome":"BOTH_ADMISSIBLE_ADDITIVE","additive_intent_support":"SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The consonantal facts are accurate on evaluator knowledge (requiring verification): Prov 7:20 spells keseh with aleph, Ps 81:3 with he, and Job 26:9's form is written like keseh though pointed as throne; several modern versions read 'full moon' at Job 26:9, so the additive hearing there has independent support beyond this book. Both hearings satisfy all five gate items; Ps 89:36-37 supplies contextual evidence that throne-and-luminary belong together prior to any wordplay.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None; the immediate contexts (cloud covering a face; a seat among the lights) positively tolerate both hearings.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Evidence that the Prov 7:20 aleph spelling is a scribal variant rather than a stable orthography, or that keseh is a loanword unrelated to kasah, would weaken the two-spellings-one-root claim."},{"claim":"Proverbs 31:10-31, rendered on the bare letters (palms/kaph, circuit/pelekh, appointed portion/choq, covenant's meat/teref, 'in double' shnayim with LXX/Vulgate support, halal = shine, shachaq under 'laugheth'), additively portrays the full moon — rising at night, lamp never out, husband the sun known in the gates among the elders — while fully preserving the virtuous-wife reading.","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","received_or_base_reading":"The pointed text: an exemplary human wife (scarlet-clothed household, spindle, human husband in the city gates)","proposed_additive_reading":"The same consonants simultaneously paint the faithful-witness moon of the background chapter, with each departure an attested sense of the identical letters","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"PASS","admission_outcome":"BOTH_ADMISSIBLE_ADDITIVE","additive_intent_support":"POSSIBLE_NOT_ESTABLISHED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The itemized departures overwhelmingly use attested senses with independent occurrences cited (kaph vs yad distinguished by the poet himself in vv. 19-20; choq as 'set time' Job 14:13; teref with covenant Ps 111:5; shnayim 'double' carried by the pre-Masoretic LXX and Vulgate — genuine early evidence, requiring verification). The cumulative pattern (a light that rises at nightfall, burns all night, is made to shine by her husband, with no moon-word ever used) plus the Song 6:9-10 parallel makes active additive intent possible; but pattern-accumulation after seeing the target is exactly what Rule 4 discounts, and no single line compels the lunar hearing.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None; nothing in the poem linguistically excludes the additive portrait, and the chapter preserves the base reading intact.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"An ancient witness (version, targum, or early interpretation) reading any Prov 31 line lunarly would establish intent; a demonstration that a key hinge (e.g., kethib 'in the night' at v. 18) is textually secondary would weaken the portrait."},{"claim":"Proverbs 3:13-20 rendered from the letters ('bright' yaqar as at Job 31:26 of the moon, 'established' konen as Ps 8:3 of moon and stars, shachaqim as Ps 89:37's witness-sky, tamak the holding-fast verb, 'length and appropriateness of days' via arik) reads wisdom's poem as the same sky-portrait.","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","received_or_base_reading":"The pointed text: personified Wisdom with riches, honour, pleasantness, and peace","proposed_additive_reading":"The identical consonants also carry luminary vocabulary tying wisdom's poem to the moon-and-stars texts","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"PASS","admission_outcome":"BOTH_ADMISSIBLE_ADDITIVE","additive_intent_support":"POSSIBLE_NOT_ESTABLISHED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"Most renderings are the KJV's own glosses from other verses (yaqar 'brightness' Job 31:26; konen 'ordained' Ps 8:3; baqa Gen 7:11), so the gate is met for those items. One item is weaker: 'appropriateness of days' rests on Aramaic arik (Ezra 4:14) applied to Hebrew orek without addressing whether that sense is productive in Hebrew of this period and genre — a gate item 2/4 question the appendix flags but does not resolve. Additive intent for the poem as a whole remains suggestive, not demonstrated.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None identified.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A Hebrew (not merely Aramaic) attestation of the 'fitting/suit' sense for the '-r-k root, or removal of that single item, would close the only gate-relevant weakness; the rest of the rendering stands or falls on the same evidence as the Prov 31 portrait."},{"claim":"Psalm 81:3 names one day, not two — 'blow with the new-moon trumpet in the full moon for the day of our festival sacrifice' — so the full moon is the head of the month, the feast-day of Num 10:10 and 28:11; the LXX's eusēmos ('well-marked') day supports the conspicuous phase.","category":"HISTORICAL_OR_ASTRONOMICAL","received_or_base_reading":"Two appointed moments (new moon and full-moon feast) or a temporal parallel: 'blow the trumpet at the new moon, at the full moon, on our feast day'; the month begins at conjunction/first crescent per the received calendar","proposed_additive_reading":"chodesh and keseh denote the same day; the month itself begins at the full moon","relationship":"CONTRADICTORY_RIVALS","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"UNDERDETERMINED","admission_outcome":"UNDERDETERMINED","additive_intent_support":"NOT_APPLICABLE","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"keseh = full moon is well supported (Prov 7:20; versional evidence; the LXX eusēmos citation checks out on evaluator knowledge, requiring verification). The absence of a vav is a real textual fact. But the load-bearing rendering — bachodesh as 'with the new-moon trumpet' — inverts the standard idiom taqa' be-shofar (where the bet marks the instrument, here attached to shofar's rival) and cites no attested parallel; and apposition of bachodesh/bakeseh is possible but not demonstrated against the natural two-time reading. This is not an additive claim: full-moon month-start and conjunction/crescent month-start are exclusive rivals, and the chapter asserts the winner ('the full moon *is* the head of the month') beyond what it documents, while elsewhere deferring the calendar case to another book.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"No decisive exclusion either way in the packet; Amos 8:5 (new moon as a distinct commerce-stopping day) is consistent with both models.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_OVERCLAIM","outcome_changing_evidence":"An attested parallel for taqa' + be-X shofar with instrumental force on the modifier, comparative Semitic evidence on ks' as a mid-month vs month-head term, or a documented ancient calendar beginning months at the full moon would move this from underdetermined; per Rule 1 the received reading should meanwhile be labeled 'traditional reading; comparison underdetermined.'"},{"claim":"Ezekiel 46:1's east gate opens on sabbath and new-moon days; astronomically, exactly one lunar phase rises in the east at sunset — the full moon — so the true light 'enters by the door' while the crescent is hunted low in the west, the thief's entrance (John 10:1).","category":"HISTORICAL_OR_ASTRONOMICAL","received_or_base_reading":"Ezekiel 46:1 legislates a temple gate; the new-moon day on the received calendar is conjunction/crescent, when nothing rises in the east at dusk","proposed_additive_reading":"The sky's tabernacle has an east gate; the full moon's east-at-sunset rising on the month's opening day enacts the ordinance, supporting the full-moon month-start","relationship":"CONTRADICTORY_RIVALS","base_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","additive_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","admission_outcome":"NOT_APPLICABLE","additive_intent_support":"NOT_APPLICABLE","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The astronomical facts are correct on evaluator knowledge (requiring verification): the full moon rises in the east at sunset and sets near sunrise; the young crescent appears low in the west at dusk. This is not a vocalization claim, so no admission gate applies. But as a consilience argument it presupposes the contested calendar of the Psalm 81:3 claim: only if the new-moon day is the full-moon day does anything 'enter the east gate' that evening. The same hypothesis is thus both supported by and required to read the passage — a dependency Rule 4 stage 6 demands be mapped, and the rival conjunction-start joint model is never stated or compared.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None; the symbolic mapping is not linguistically excluded, but it is not independent evidence either.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"An explicit stage-4 comparison: what the conjunction-start model predicts at Ezek 46:1 versus the full-moon model, with the dependency on the Psalm 81:3 claim acknowledged; without it this argument contributes no nonduplicative weight."},{"claim":"The unkeyed pearl parable resolves as: the one pearl = the full moon = a gate of the city (Rev 21:21, each gate of one pearl) = the appointed time of meeting; the merchant sells all to buy his entry at the King's gate (Isa 33:6 welding treasure and times).","category":"THEOLOGICAL_SYNTHESIS","received_or_base_reading":"Traditional readings: the pearl is Christ, the gospel, or the church, purchased at the cost of all","proposed_additive_reading":"The pearl is the full moon as sign of the moedim, the gate of entry to the kingdom's appointed meetings","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","additive_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","admission_outcome":"NOT_APPLICABLE","additive_intent_support":"POSSIBLE_NOT_ESTABLISHED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET"],"reason":"A symbolic synthesis, not a vocalization; the gate does not apply. Its consilience is genuine and largely noncircular: Rev 21:21's emphatic 'each one gate of one pearl,' the pearl's oneness/roundness/whiteness/water-birth, and the moon's fourth-day appointment for moedim (background, frozen) unify independent details the base-only readings leave uncollected. But the chapter itself concedes the chain 'is a reading... offered to be tested,' and no rival joint model (pearl = Christ, which also explains oneness and great price via 1 Cor 3:11-type uniqueness) is compared at full strength, so intent remains possible, not established.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None; the reading preserves rather than contradicts the base parable and even the Christ-reading (the gate-language of John 10 is compatible).","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A one-paragraph comparison showing which textual facts (one-per-gate, roundness, whiteness, the merchandise thread) the strongest traditional model explains and which it leaves unexplained would convert compatibility into measured comparative gain."},{"claim":"Daniel 7:9 rendered from the Aramaic: the thrones were 'set in place' (not 'cast down'); Atik Yomin also hearable as 'Foremost of Days'; the plural 'wheels' is an intensive — 'the wheel complete' — so the vision draws the white full-moon thrones set in their stations.","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","received_or_base_reading":"KJV 'the thrones were cast down'; Ancient of Days; plural wheels as a count","proposed_additive_reading":"Thrones placed like lights in stations; the One at the head of the days; the perfect circle of fire","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"PASS","additive_admission":"UNDERDETERMINED","admission_outcome":"UNDERDETERMINED","additive_intent_support":"POSSIBLE_NOT_ESTABLISHED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The first component passes cleanly: Aramaic remiv is 'were placed/set,' and modern versions concur (evaluator knowledge, requiring verification) — the chapter's footnote handles it properly. The 'Foremost of Days' hearing from the 'tq root's 'move on/advance' sense is a possible wordplay but undocumented against the well-attested 'aged/ancient' sense of attiq. The 'intensive plural = the wheel complete' invokes no attested Aramaic grammatical rule and cites none; as stated it fails gate item 4's documentation requirement, though the base reading is unharmed.","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None for the first two; for the intensive plural, the parallel concrete plurals in the verse (thrones, streams, thousands) weigh against a purely intensive reading but do not strictly exclude it.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A grammar citation attesting intensive/amplificative plural for concrete nouns in Biblical Aramaic, or deletion of that clause; a lexical citation for 'tq = advance applied titularly."},{"claim":"Matthew 7:6's pearls trampled by swine reads whole if the pearl is the appointed times: the nations tread down the holy things and the holy city 'until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled' (Luke 21:24; Dan 8:13; Rev 11:2), matching Daniel 7:25's plan to change times and laws.","category":"THEOLOGICAL_SYNTHESIS","received_or_base_reading":"Pearls before swine = holy teaching not given to those who will profane it","proposed_additive_reading":"The specific holy thing trampled is the appointed times, handed to nations who will not keep them","relationship":"NONCONTRADICTORY_ADDITIVE","base_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","additive_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","admission_outcome":"NOT_APPLICABLE","additive_intent_support":"POSSIBLE_NOT_ESTABLISHED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET"],"reason":"A symbolic application, not a vocalization. The trampling-and-times word-cluster (Luke 21:24's 'times,' Dan 7:25 from the background packet) gives the reading real texture, but it inherits its force entirely from the pearl-as-times identification of the previous claim; it adds a coherent corollary rather than independent support, and the chapter presents it as such ('the warning reads whole').","affirmative_exclusion_evidence":"None; the general reading is preserved and the specific one is compatible with it.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"None needed for its status as a dependent corollary; it rises or falls with the pearl-gate synthesis."}],"reciprocal_consilience":{"verdict":"VALID_BUT_INCOMPLETE","independent_background_support":"The background packet is genuinely frozen without the target: chapter 29 derives sun=Father, moon=faithful witness (Ps 89:36-37; Rev 1:5), stars=righteous (Dan 12:3), twelve gates/tribes/Mazzaroth, and elders among the host from its own texts; chapter 30 establishes the keseh/kisse' consonantal identity (Prov 7:20; Ps 81:3; Job 26:9) and the counterfeit dark-conjunction thesis from Isaiah 14 without citing the pearl chapter.","incremental_target_evidence":"The target supplies facts not used to build the background: peninim under the KJV's 'rubies'; the letter-identical clause ki-tov sachrah shared by Prov 3:14 and 31:18; the Prov 31 portrait's night-rising, all-night lamp, husband-in-the-gates cluster; Rev 21:21's each-gate-of-one-pearl; Ezek 46:1's east gate; Song 6:9-10's fair-as-the-moon signature. These are nonduplicative and jointly more expected under the household-of-lights hypothesis than under a purely domestic reading.","dependency_or_duplication_risk":"Two mapped risks: (1) the keseh/kisse' identity was already established and used in chapter 30 ('the last chapter stood on that identity'); when the target re-invokes it as confirmation, it must count only its new loci (Prov 7:20 spelling, Job 26:9) and not the identity itself twice. (2) The full-moon month-start hypothesis is used to interpret Ps 81:3 and Ezek 46:1 and is simultaneously claimed to be supported by them; without independent calendrical evidence (deferred by the chapter to another book), those two loci supply near-zero nonduplicative weight to each other.","strongest_base_only_or_excluding_model":"Pearl = Christ/the kingdom itself, bought at the cost of all; Prov 31 = an exemplary human wife whose portrait echoes Wisdom's by ordinary intra-book style; Ps 81:3 = two related festival moments (new moon and full-moon feast); Ezek 46:1 = temple liturgy with no celestial referent. This model explains the parable's price and oneness, the poems' surface sense, and the ordinance with no added hypotheses.","comparative_result":"The received-plus-additive model explains, without contradicting the base readings, several facts the base-only model leaves as coincidence: the letter-identical merchandise clause; the shared spelling of throne and full moon in exactly the covered/filled semantic field; Rev 21:21's emphatic one-pearl-per-gate; the portrait's precise nocturnal timetable with no moon-word; Song 6:9-10 praising the one-above-the-daughters woman as the moon. The base-only model requires fewer assumptions but unifies less. The additive symbolic core therefore carries positive noncircular gain. The calendrical sub-claim (full-moon month-start) does not share this status: within the packet it is underdetermined and partly self-supporting.","reversal_evidence":"The claimed consilience would weaken or reverse if: peninim is shown to be color-marked red (Lam 4:7); the Prov 7:20 aleph spelling proves a mere scribal variant; keseh is demonstrated (e.g., by comparative Semitic ks') to denote specifically the mid-month day distinct from chodesh, re-splitting Ps 81:3; or an early witness reads the Prov 31 portrait in a way that excludes the lunar overtone."},"category_error_audit":[{"possible_error":"Rejecting a symbolic derivation, astronomical fact, or theological synthesis for failing the vocalization admission gate","present_in_chapter":false,"explanation":"Not applicable to the chapter itself, and this audit has applied the Rule 3 gate only to actual vocalization/lexical claims (kisse'/keseh, the itemized poem departures, Ps 81:3 syntax, Dan 7:9), grading the pearl-gate synthesis and the east-gate astronomy under Rules 4-5 instead."},{"possible_error":"Forcing compatible readings into an exclusive contest (Rule 5 violation)","present_in_chapter":false,"explanation":"The chapter is exemplary here: it repeatedly states that the housewife and the light 'both run at once' and that the plain reading is not unseated; it never asks the additive hearing to defeat the base."},{"possible_error":"Appeal to majority or authority as proof","present_in_chapter":true,"explanation":"The Psalm 81:3 paragraph lists NKJV, ESV, NASB, JPS, and Smith's as reading 'full moon' and notes the KJV 'stands nearly alone' — rhetorically a majority-of-versions appeal whose members are not shown to be independent lineages. The underlying lexical data (Prov 7:20; the LXX) do the legitimate work; the roll-call adds status, not evidence."},{"possible_error":"Counting the same evidence twice across background and target (circularity)","present_in_chapter":true,"explanation":"The keseh/kisse' identity established in chapter 30 is re-deployed here as confirmation ('the letters confirm it'), and the full-moon calendar hypothesis both interprets and is claimed to be supported by Ps 81:3 and Ezek 46:1. The symbolic core survives because the target adds genuinely new loci, but the calendrical sub-claim's support is partly self-referential."},{"possible_error":"Treating a lexicon (Strong's) as a multiplied or decisive witness","present_in_chapter":true,"explanation":"Strong's is cited repeatedly (peninim, kaph, pelekh, keseh, arik) as the attestation source. It is one lineage, and for peninim it records a conjecture ('probably a pearl'). Most items are independently anchored by KJV renderings at other verses, which mitigates but does not remove the single-lineage dependence for peninim."},{"possible_error":"Using the New Testament to redefine Old Testament vocabulary backward","present_in_chapter":false,"explanation":"The derivation direction respects the frozen premises: peninim, keseh, the moedim, and the gate architecture are derived from Torah, Proverbs, Psalms, and Ezekiel first; Matthew 13, Revelation 21, and John 10 are used as confirmation and referent-disclosure, consistent with premises 2, 5, and 8."},{"possible_error":"Smuggling a consonantal variant into a vocalization comparison","present_in_chapter":false,"explanation":"Every listed departure in 'Every Word Weighed' works on the same consonants (including the kethib at 31:18 and the shanim/shnayim repointing); no reading requires different letters, and the chapter flags where the KJV, not the alternate, departs from the plain word (shesh 'white linen')."}],"claims_pass_as_written":["The letter-identical clause ki-tov sachrah in Prov 3:14 and Prov 31:18 (the verbatim-quotation fact, as distinct from the 'exactly three places' exhaustiveness claim)","Daniel 7:9 thrones 'were set in place,' not 'cast down' (Aramaic remiv; concurred by modern versions)","The astronomical facts as facts: the full moon rises in the east at sunset and sets near dawn; only a moon at conjunction can occlude the sun; the young crescent appears low in the west at dusk"],"claims_both_admissible_additive":["kisse'/keseh: the throne-word's full-moon hearing (Prov 7:20; Ps 81:3; Job 26:9), with additive intent SUPPORTED at Job 26:9","The Prov 31:10-31 additive full-moon portrait over the preserved virtuous-wife reading, including shnayim 'double' with LXX/Vulgate support","The Prov 3:13-20 additive luminary rendering over the preserved Wisdom reading (except the arik item, which needs documentation)","The 'good merchandise' thread as an additive linkage of wisdom, bride, and parable"],"claims_additive_intent_underdetermined":["Active lunar intent for the Prov 31 portrait as a whole (pattern suggestive;
